title: Prompt retreat trigger notebook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for designing and iterating on a lightweight 'retreat' mechanism for prompt-based fallbacks. Idea: detect early signs of answer drift or latency spikes and trigger a staged retreat (simpler prompt / cached response / smaller model) instead of full failover. Keep notes, few-shot templates, failure cases, and experiment log here.

High-level retreat states (working names):
- monitor -> soften -> retreat-1 -> retreat-2 -> cached/notify
- soften: reduce instruction strictness, fewer constraints, shorten context window
- retreat-1: switch to smaller-size variant (faster but slightly less capable)
- retreat-2: use deterministic template or cached exemplar + attribution

Trigger signals (heuristic list):
- token-generation latency > SLA threshold (e.g., 95th p95 > 800ms)
- jitter in per-token latency (sudden 2x increase vs 1-minute rolling median)
- divergence score: LM surprisals increase by X (proxy: drop in top-p mass)
- hallucination proxy: higher repetition / low-entropy answers flagged by eval policy model
- eval-feedback: user-reported quality drop (manual) within last 10m for route

Questions / unknowns:
- How to compute divergence cheaply in runtime? (KV-cache diagnostics or softmax mass?)
- Should retreat be per-route or global per model instance? (prefer per-route)
- Do we penalize retreat frequency (avoid flapping)? Add cooldown of 5m?

Few-shot prototype templates (examples to try):
BASE (do-not-retreat) prompt:
"""You are a helpful assistant. Answer concisely and accurately. If you are unsure, say 'I don't know' and ask for clarification."""

SOFTEN (reduce constraints):
"""You are a helpful assistant. Give a short, pragmatic answer. If unsure, provide plausible approaches and label uncertainty. Avoid long speculative chains."""

CACHED EXEMPLAR (last-resort):
"""Use this verified exemplar if it matches the user's topic: [exemplar-id: sales-play-2025-v2]. If exemplar doesn't match closely, reply: 'I'm retrieving a verified answer; please hold' and fall back to notify."""

Few-shot set for sensitive hallucination-prone prompts:
- Q1 -> exemplar answer (annotated with sources)
- Q2 -> exemplar answer (annotated)
- Q3 -> short answer + explicit "I may be wrong" tag

Failure cases seen in ad-hoc tests (notes):
- Run 2026-02-22-R1: long-context legal Qs -> model hallucinates statutes (hallucination-rate ~0.42 by manual check). Retreat-1 (smaller model) reduced hallucination but lost entity resolution.
- Run 2026-02-28-R3: high-concurrency spike -> token latency p95 jumped 3x. Softening prompt reduced average tokens by 15% but user satisfaction dropped.
- Run 2026-03-03-R2: iterative Q chain -> model began repeating loop after 3 turns. Cached exemplar prevented loop but produced outdated guidance.

Simple experiment matrix (to run):
- A/B: baseline vs softened prompt under synthetic latency spike (simulate slower token generation). Metrics: p95 latency, user-rated helpfulness (1-5), hallucination flag rate.
- Time-series: apply retreat with cooldowns {2m,5m,10m} and measure flapping frequency and cumulative quality.

Lightweight instrumentation ideas:
- per-request 'retreat_score' computed as weighted sum of normalized signals (latency_z + hallucination_proxy + recent_errors). Thresholds tuned conservatively.
- emit 'retreat_decision' trace to tracing layer with chosen state and reason codes.

Run log (notes):
- 2026-02-25: prototyped 'soften' template and ran 200 synthetic queries. Observed 12% token reduction; hallucination proxy unchanged.
- 2026-03-02: integrated retreat_score into local harness RNW-4592; initial threshold 1.4 triggered ~4% requests -> investigate false positives.

Operational notes / playbook snippets (for future doc):
- When retreat triggers, log full input + model chosen + immediate follow-up decision (notify, cache, user message).
- Provide a transparent fallback message option: e.g., 'I'm using a faster/shorter answer to keep latency low; ask for more details if you'd like a deeper answer.'

To-dos / next steps (personal):
- [ ] Run A/B with real user prompts from hosting-api (anonymized).
- [ ] Add cheap surprisal proxy (topk mass) to runtime and test false-positive rate.
- [ ] Draft short Confluence page summarizing technique and safety/product considerations. Link RNW-4592.
- [ ] Pair with SRE to add trace fields: retreat_score, retreat_state, reason_code.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep retreat conservative; users prefer consistent capability over occasional speed wins.
- Consider per-customer sensitivity: enterprise customers might opt out of retreating to smaller models.

End of scratchpad. Save iterations here. If this turns into a runbook, move to shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/ later.
